notes:
I couldn't write the Job 8 notes, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

My first attempt to open the pages (Enduring Word, the Bible Hub pages for Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit and Barnes, and the NET Bible notes) failed. The tool said I had no more research calls left for this turn, and a second try gave the same error. My other tools have no internet access, so I couldn't search or open any of the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and to give a URL for every point. Writing notes from memory would break both rules, so I've left them out instead of filling the gaps myself.

If you ask again in a new message, my research access may be available again. I'd then work through:
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Job 8, and Bible Hub or StudyLight for Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Barnes and Matthew Henry. Precept Austin may also have an entry.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon (spurgeon.org), Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God and GTY. These are likely to bear on Bildad's view that suffering always follows from sin, his comments on Job's children in v. 4, and how far his "true" statements (vv. 3, 20) can be trusted given God's verdict on the friends in Job 42:7.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes for textual and translation questions (for example vv. 17–19), Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, and New Advent or the Catholic and Orthodox sites for older Church Fathers' readings. I'd also check Got Questions and similar sites for anything on prosperity teaching that uses vv. 6–7.
